info.title: Kimlik API
info.description: The Management API manages the users, organizations, access and clients of a Kimlik installation; calls take an access token for the `kimlik` scope, issued to a service client or an administrator, carrying the permission each operation names. The Account API under `/me` acts for the signed-in user. Errors are RFC 9457 problem details with a stable, machine-readable `code`.

ApiResourceResponse.description:
An API protected by Kimlik tokens. Clients request its `scope`; the access tokens they get name its
`audience`, which the API checks. The system resource `kimlik` is Kimlik's own API.

AuditEventResponse.description:
A security-relevant action. `action` reads `resource.past_tense_verb`, such as `user.suspended`.
People are referenced by ID only, so the trail outlives their personal data.

AuthenticatorCodeRequest.description: A code from the authenticator app, proving the request comes from someone holding it.

AuthenticatorSetupResponse.description:
A new authenticator key. Add it to an authenticator app, by scanning `otpAuthUri` as a QR code or typing
`secret`, then confirm with a code from the app.

ClientResponse.description:
An application that requests tokens. `scopes` are what it may request; `roles` are the global
roles of a service client.

ClientSecretResponse.description: A new client secret, shown only this once. The previous secret stops working at once.

ClientType.description: The kind of application, which decides how it gets tokens.

scope.description:
The scope clients request, such as `orders`: lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `:`, `_` and
`-`, starting with a letter. It cannot be changed later.

audience.description: The `aud` of the access tokens, such as `orders-api` or a URL; the scope when omitted. It cannot be changed later.

displayName.description: Shown to users on the consent screen, such as "Manage your orders".

clientId.description: Letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, such as `web` or `billing-worker`. It cannot be changed later.

firstParty.description: First-party apps are your own and skip the consent screen; third-party apps ask users for consent.

redirectUris.description: Where users return after signing in; required for apps that sign users in, and matched exactly.

postLogoutRedirectUris.description: Where users may return after signing out.

scopes.description:
What the client may request: `openid`, `profile`, `email` and `offline_access` for apps
that sign users in, and the scopes of API resources.

roles.description: Keys of the global roles of a service client.

requireOrganization.description:
Whether every sign-in happens in an organization. When the authorization request names none, the user
chooses one of theirs.

CreatedClientResponse.description: A new client and, for web and service clients, its secret. The secret is shown only this once.

key.description: Lowercase letters, digits, `_` and `-`, such as `max_projects`. It cannot be changed later.

roles.description: Keys of the organization roles the invited user gets on joining.

slug.description: Up to 64 lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens, such as `acme`.

requireMfa.description: Whether signing in to the organization takes a second factor.

key.description: `resource:action` in lowercase, such as `invoices:read`. It cannot be changed later.
Lowercase letters, digits, `_` and `-`, such as `pro`. It cannot be changed later.

features.description: Feature values by key, such as `{ "export_pdf": true, "max_projects": 3 }`. Features left out are off, or zero.

key.description: Lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`, starting with a letter. It cannot be changed later.

trialEndsAt.description: When a trial ends; the subscription is trialing until then.

currentPeriodEnd.description: When the paid period ends; omit it for a subscription without an end.

externalReference.description: The subscription's ID in the billing system.

locale.description: Preferred language as a BCP 47 tag, such as `tr` or `en`.

emailVerified.description: Marks the address as verified, for example when it was verified by another system.

CreateUserRequest.description: Creates a user. Without a password, the user sets one through the password reset flow.

DeleteAccountRequest.description: Deleting the account takes the password, so a stolen token alone cannot do it.

EntitlementsResponse.description:
What a user or an organization is entitled to: the plan in effect, from its current subscription or the default
plan, and the value of every feature. `plan` is `null` when there is neither.

FeatureResponse.description: An entitlement the application defines; plans set a value for it.

InvitationResponse.description: An invitation to join an organization, sent by email. Accepting it adds the roles to the new member.

MemberResponse.description: A member of an organization and the organization roles they hold there.

MyInvitationResponse.description: A pending invitation to the signed-in user's verified email address.

MyOrganizationResponse.description: An organization the signed-in user belongs to, with their roles and permissions in it.

OrganizationResponse.description: A group of users, such as a company, workspace or team. Clients may name it by ID or slug.

`null` on the last page. Cursors are opaque.

PermissionResponse.description: A permission. System permissions (`kimlik.*`) guard Kimlik itself and cannot be changed.

PlanResponse.description:
A plan and the value of every feature in it: `true` or `false` for boolean features, and a maximum
for limits, where `null` means unlimited.

audience.description: The scope when omitted. It cannot be changed once the API resource exists.

type.description: It cannot be changed once the client exists.

requireOrganization.description: Whether every sign-in happens in an organization.

roles.description: Keys of a service client's global roles; when omitted, an existing client keeps its roles.

clientSecret.description:
The secret of a web or service client, at least 16 characters. When omitted, a new client gets a random secret
(regenerate it through the API to learn one) and an existing client keeps its secret. Never exported. In a file
applied at startup, `${Some:Setting}` reads the secret from configuration, such as the environment variable
`Some__Setting`.

type.description: It cannot be changed once the feature exists.

features.description:
Feature values by key: `true` or `false`, and a maximum or `null` (unlimited) for limits. Features
left out are off, or zero. When the property is omitted, an existing plan keeps its values.

scope.description: It cannot be changed once the role exists.

permissions.description: Keys of the role's permissions; when omitted, an existing role keeps its permissions.

$schema.description: The JSON Schema of the document, for editor completion; ignored by Kimlik.

ProvisioningDocument.description:
The access model of an installation as one document: permissions, roles, features, plans, API resources and clients.
Applying it creates what is missing and updates what differs, and never deletes. Each item is described in
full, except that role permissions, client roles and client secrets are left alone when omitted.

ProvisioningResult.description: What applying a provisioning document changed.

RecoveryCodesResponse.description: Single-use codes for signing in without the authenticator app. They are shown only this once.

RoleResponse.description: A role and the keys of its permissions. System roles (`kimlik-*`) cannot be changed.

SessionResponse.description: An application the user signed in to, which can get tokens on their behalf until the session is revoked.

SetPermissionsRequest.description: Replaces the permissions of a role.

SetRolesRequest.description: Replaces the global roles of a user or a client.

SubscriptionResponse.description: A user's or an organization's plan over time, as the billing system reports it.

UpdateApiResourceRequest.description: Changes an API resource with JSON Merge Patch semantics: an omitted property keeps its value and `null` clears it.

displayName.description: The new name; a client always has one, so it cannot be cleared.

UpdateClientRequest.description:
Changes a client with JSON Merge Patch semantics: an omitted property keeps its value, and `null` empties
a list. Lists are replaced as a whole.

UpdateFeatureRequest.description: Changes a feature with JSON Merge Patch semantics: an omitted property keeps its value and `null` clears it.

slug.description: A new slug; clients that use the old one must switch to it.

requireMfa.description: Whether signing in to the organization takes a second factor.

UpdateOrganizationRequest.description: Changes an organization with JSON Merge Patch semantics: an omitted property keeps its value.

UpdatePermissionRequest.description: Changes a permission with JSON Merge Patch semantics: an omitted property keeps its value and `null` clears it.

isArchived.description: Archived plans keep their subscribers but take no new ones.

UpdatePlanRequest.description: Changes a plan with JSON Merge Patch semantics: an omitted property keeps its value; `features` replaces them all.

name.description: The new name; a role always has one, so it cannot be cleared.

UpdateRoleRequest.description: Changes a role with JSON Merge Patch semantics: an omitted property keeps its value and `null` clears it.

plan.description: A plan key, to change the plan.

UpdateSubscriptionRequest.description:
Changes a subscription with JSON Merge Patch semantics: an omitted property keeps its value and `null` clears
it. Setting `status` to trialing or active resumes a canceled subscription.

UpdateUserRequest.description:
Changes the profile with JSON Merge Patch semantics (RFC 7396): omitted properties keep their value and
`null` clears one.

provider.description: The provider's name in Kimlik, such as `google`.

providerDisplayName.description: The provider's name for people, such as `Google`.

UserLoginResponse.description: An account at another provider, such as Google, that the user signs in with.

Bearer.description: An access token from the token endpoint, for the `kimlik` scope.
